statement_record.book: A double category (Ehresmann) is a set that is the arrow-set of two different composition operations which together satisfy the interchange law; example: the commutative squares in Set under horizontal and vertical pasting form a double category.
statement_record.intree: Class DoubleCategory (Theory/DoubleCategory.v:162): strict vertical Category dcat, horizontal 1-cells dhor, square setoids dsq with boundary coercion, strict vertical composition, horizontal pasting dsq_hcomp with the interchange field dinterchange, and WEAK (globular-iso) associator/unitors. Construction/Sq.v:47: Sq C, the commuting-squares double category over any category C with dsq h u v k := k ∘ u ≈ v ∘ h.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker as a rendering of MacLane's definition: the class is the PSEUDO (Grandis-Paré) double category — typed squares instead of one arrow-set, horizontal composition only weakly associative/unital, and explicitly coherence-only in scope (its header defers horizontal identity squares on verticals, the unit half of interchange, and coherence naturality). MacLane's strict Ehresmann notion is not separately defined; it is only exhibited through instances with degenerate coherence. The interchange law itself is the dinterchange field, and the book's example is intree-stronger: Sq C exists for ANY base category C, subsuming commutative squares in Set.
